study.question: Does the validation ranking effect of shared-row role projection survive preservation of each COMPLETE baseline row-gradient norm under the fixed half-scale rule, or can its complete-gradient magnitude change account for the effect? The current projection AUC0.6151301693553729 exceeds no-surgery r0012-scale_half by only0.00002798084788568911, worsens Logloss by0.0000075492803423837795 and costs33.06913763284683 additional wall seconds. The larger projection-minus-product-norm-control gain0.00025450792496473085 uses a control that itself loses to no surgery. That control matches q+h versus projected product-role sums before other embedding paths are added; it does not match complete gradients. This is a bounded attribution follow-up, not the unexposed paired-seed experiment proposed by prior memory.
study.hypothesis: Under the inherited half-scale rule, projection direction contributes a positive single-seed AUC effect even after complete-row gradient magnitudes are factored out: D-N>0 and P-M>0. Let q,h denote product-only query/history gradients aggregated by shared category/brand row, O the other-path gradient, G=O+q+h, t the inherited symmetric negative-inner-product projection and P=G+(t-q-h). At common eligible nondegenerate rows define N=G; D=P*||G||/||P||; M=G*||P||/||G||; P retains both direction and norm of the hypothetical projection. Use the same four-cell code with a stopped linear training-loss correction to realize these complete-gradient targets. All statements are prospective. Positive scores would support this local raw-gradient contrast only; actual Adam-update mediation remains unmeasured.
